description:
User direction 2026-11-20 (verbatim): "i see that we have frequent problems with the distiller tests due to _exact_ pins. lets change that to a ceiling that we can occasionally lower."

Why: tests/distill_telemetry_test.rs's the_distiller_compiles_inside_the_product_drive_budget asserts assert_eq! on (largest drive requests, total requests, drives) and on (DERIVATIONS, READS_HANDED). Every PR that moves the compile by even one request conflicts with every other PR that does (#748, #806, #807, #813, #814 on 2026-11-19/20), and each needs a rebase plus a re-measure.

Change: each figure is a ceiling. The test asserts measured <= ceiling per component (largest drive, total requests, drive count, derivations, reads handed) and prints the measured values, so a fall passes without editing the file. A rise above a ceiling still fails and still needs the user's authorization to raise it; PRODUCT_DRIVE_BUDGET (50,000) stays the hard bound on the largest drive. Ceilings are lowered occasionally, in a PR of their own or alongside a change that lowers them, to the measured value on develop. The failure message says which component crossed its ceiling, by how much, and that a rise is investigated first.

Docs: update the pin rule wherever the agent docs describe distiller pins (fall = lower the pin -> fall passes; lower the ceiling occasionally; rise above ceiling = investigate + user authorization). One present-tense comment at most per ceiling (fz-fzb rule).

Done when: a PR that lowers the distiller's compile cost passes the test unchanged; a PR that raises any component above its ceiling fails with a message naming it; ceilings set to develop's measured values at the time of the change; docs updated; gate green.
title: The distiller's compile-cost pins are ceilings, lowered now and then
